message.content:
I don’t have real‑time data built into this chat, so I can’t tell you the exact AQI for Los Angeles at this moment.  
Here’s what you can do to get the most up‑to‑date information:

| Source | How to use it | Typical data |
|--------|---------------|--------------|
| **AirNow** (U.S. EPA) | Visit <https://www.airnow.gov/> and enter “Los Angeles” or use the “Live Air Quality Map.” | Current AQI, pollutant breakdown (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃, NO₂, CO), forecast. |
| **AQICN** (World Air Quality Index) | Go to <https://aqicn.org/city/los-angeles/> | Real‑time AQI, historical trends, alerts. |
| **Weather Apps** (e.g., Weather.com, AccuWeather, or your phone’s weather widget) | Search “Los Angeles” and look for the “Air Quality” section. | AQI, pollutant levels, health recommendations. |
| **Local News** (e.g., LA Times, KABC) | Check their weather or environment sections. | Often report on smog alerts or health advisories. |

**Quick tip:** If you’re looking for a quick snapshot, the AirNow website usually shows the AQI in a large number with a color code (green = good, yellow = moderate, orange = unhealthy for sensitive groups, red = unhealthy, etc.). If you’re planning outdoor activities, you can also check the forecast for the next few days to see if smog is expected to worsen.

Let me know if you’d like help interpreting the AQI numbers or if you want to set up a notification system for when the air quality drops below a certain threshold!
